title: Modeling and Analysis of Time Series Data

gradingBreakdown.component: Peer reviews of midterm projects (2, individual)
Peer reviews of final projects (2, individual)

weeklyTopics: Time series models: estimating trend and autocovariance
Stationarity, white noise, and basic time series models
Linear time series models and the algebra of ARMA models
Parameter estimation and model identification for ARMA models
Extending the ARMA model: seasonality and trend
Smoothing in the time and frequency domains
Case study: association between unemployment and mortality
Introduction to partially observed Markov process (POMP) models
Simulation-based inference for epidemiological dynamics via the pomp R package
Likelihood for POMP models: theory and practice
Case study: polio dynamics with covariates, seasonality, over-dispersion
Case study: financial volatility, POMP model with observations driving latent dynamics
Case study: measles dynamics revealed in long time series
workloadNotes: Weekly homeworks graded to a rubric; a randomly-assigned group midterm project plus two individual anonymous peer reviews; groups re-randomized for a group final project plus two more individual peer reviews; class participation tracked via a rubric. Explicit source-attribution and GenAI-use disclosure requirements on every homework and project.
prerequisitesText: Recommended: theoretical and applied statistics (STATS 500 and prior/concurrent STATS 511, or STATS 413 and STATS 426 with a strong math/computing background); basic linear algebra; R programming (no formal R prerequisite, but extensive R use).
textbooks: R. Shumway and D. Stoffer, Time Series Analysis and its Applications, 4th edition (2017)
